sentences.text: Researchers compared two MRI techniques for measuring water movement across the blood-brain barrier in living subjects, testing them at three different time delays after labeling the blood.
Computer simulations were also conducted to examine how the signal changes as it fades and as the labeled blood arrives during the scan.
While both methods produced similar estimates of the tissue's signal decay rate at the two longer time delays, the multi-echo method gave a lower estimate than the other method at the shortest delay.
The multi-echo technique produced clearer images with less noise, whereas the T2-prep method showed more blurring and visual errors in the raw data.

Early computer models suggest the underestimation in the multi-echo method might occur because magnetic fields distort the signal from moving blood, while the T2-prep technique is more likely to produce blurry images because it takes longer to collect the data.
